newsitem.title: USA: U.S. approves transit visit for Taiwan official.
newsitem.headline: U.S. approves transit visit for Taiwan official.

text.p: The United States has approved a request by Taiwanese Vice-President Lien Chan to transit the United States twice this week en route to and from Nicaragua, the State Department said Monday.

Spokesman Nicholas Burns said Lien would pass through Los Angeles Tuesday on his way to Managua for the inauguration Friday of President Arnoldo Aleman and spend one night in New York on Jan. 11 on his way back.
Burns told reporters that "normal procedures" would apply for such visits -- "no meetings with American officials, no public events".
The United States downgraded its ties with Taiwan after it established formal diplomatic relations with China in 1979, precluding normal government-to-government contacts.

Washington says it considers requests by senior Taiwanese officials for transit visas on a case-by-case basis. It has granted several previous such requests in recent years, provoking little more than routine criticism from China.

However, a decision to let Taiwanese President Lee Teng-hui enter the United States to attend a college reunion in June 1995 caused a major crisis with Beijing. U.S.-Chinese relations went into a nosedive from which they have only recently begun to recover.
